_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

I'm afraid this is actually consistent with python's default behaviour:
''.' is in the python path when you start the python interactive
interpreter. When you start a script, eg. pylint, that's the directory to
which the script belong which is added to the python path (python does
that, not pylint).

You should have in your PYTHONPATH the directory containing the Overlord
directory.

and `--load-plugins=Overlord.pylint` is indeed what's expected.

_Original comment by_ **Yann Dirson (BitBucket: [ydirson](http://bitbucket.org/ydirson), GitHub: @ydirson?)**:

---

Oh I see, I have dealt with the '.' case in my app's launch script and forgot about it, sorry for this.

Having to set PYTHONPATH=$PWD each time pylint is run seems however quite suboptimal. Isn't there a way to add to sys.path from pylintrc ?  What about this init-hook, which the doc touts for this use, but does not provide any example ?
`pylint --init-hook='assert False' --load-plugins=Overlord/pylint` even fails with the ImportError, while `pylint --init-hook='assert False'` triggers the assert, apparently showing the hook is just run too late for this use.

On the module-name issue, I take your statement as a confirmation that I hit a real bug too:

```
#!shell
$ PYTHONPATH=$PWD pylint --load-plugins=Overlord.pylint -E Omaha.Core
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/bin/pylint", line 3, in <module>
    run_pylint()
  ...
  File "/work/yann/games/omaha2/Overlord/pylint.py", line 4, in <module>
    from pylint.interfaces import IAstroidChecker
ImportError: No module named interfaces
$ PYTHONPATH=$PWD pylint --load-plugins=Overlord/pylint -E Omaha.Core
BOUH!
...
$
```

_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

The first problem is due to the fact that your pylint plugin module is
itself named pylint, hence it imports itself on "from pylint.interfaces
import IAstroidChecker".

The 2nd isn't clear to me, but the bug may be that it worked while it
shouldn't ;)

_Original comment by_ **Yann Dirson (BitBucket: [ydirson](http://bitbucket.org/ydirson), GitHub: @ydirson?)**:

---

OK, changing the module name fixes "." not working as separator.

But init-hook still does not get evaluated before attempting to load the plugin:

```
#!python

$ PYTHONPATH=$PWD pylint --load-plugins=Overlord.pylintx -E test.py 
BOUH!
$ pylint --init-hook='assert False' --load-plugins=Overlord.pylintx -E test.py 
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/bin/pylint", line 3, in <module>
    run_pylint()
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pylint/__init__.py", line 21, in run_pylint
    Run(sys.argv[1:])
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pylint/lint.py", line 971, in __init__
    linter.load_plugin_modules(self._plugins)
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pylint/lint.py", line 357, in load_plugin_modules
    module = load_module_from_name(modname)
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/logilab/common/modutils.py", line 125, in load_module_from_name
    return load_module_from_modpath(dotted_name.split('.'), path, use_sys)
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/logilab/common/modutils.py", line 167, in load_module_from_modpath
    mp_file, mp_filename, mp_desc = find_module(part, path)
ImportError: No module named Overlord
```

_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

ensure --init-hooks is evaluated before other options. Closes issue #166

_Original comment by_ **Yann Dirson (BitBucket: [ydirson](http://bitbucket.org/ydirson), GitHub: @ydirson?)**:

---

Wouldn't it be a good idea to make the plugin mechanism robust against the "pylint" name as well ? (thinking about something similar to "import ... as thatplugin")

_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

what do you mean by 'make the plugin mechanism robust against the "pylint"
name' ?

_Original comment by_ **Yann Dirson (BitBucket: [ydirson](http://bitbucket.org/ydirson), GitHub: @ydirson?)**:

---

I mean forbidding to use names like package.pylint to store pylint plugins is awkward, the symptoms are not trivial to link with the reason, and the limitation can surely be easily lifted.
